title: Android Back gesture should close the current UI layer before backgrounding the app
environment: Android; user described the system Back swipe from the screen edge/corner.
actual: The user reports this state-dependent Back behavior as a missing feature. Current behavior in each state has not been independently recorded.
expected: Handle each completed Android Back gesture using the first matching rule below. Perform one action per gesture, then evaluate the new state on the next gesture.

ordered_rules.action: Close the drawer and consume Back. Do not also leave edit mode or background the app.

ordered_rules.when: Drawer is closed, edit mode is active, and the virtual keyboard is open
ordered_rules.action: Close the virtual keyboard and remain in edit mode.

ordered_rules.when: Drawer is closed, edit mode is active, and the virtual keyboard is closed
ordered_rules.action: Switch to shopping mode and keep the app in the foreground.

ordered_rules.when: Drawer is closed and shopping mode is active
ordered_rules.action: Send the app to the background rather than explicitly quitting it.

acceptance_criteria: A Back gesture closes an open drawer before applying the mode or backgrounding rules.
Back in edit mode with the keyboard open hides only the keyboard; the editor remains active.
A subsequent Back with the keyboard closed switches from edit mode to shopping mode.
Back in shopping mode backgrounds the app without clearing the shopping list.
One Back gesture never cascades through multiple actions.
Returning to the app retains saved shopping data; backgrounding is not implemented as an explicit app termination.
Verify with the native Android Back gesture and real virtual keyboard, since desktop/offscreen key events alone do not establish system gesture behavior.
open_questions: When leaving edit mode, confirm the desired treatment of any unsubmitted editor text or pending item edit before implementation.
evidence: User-specified four-step Back priority in the QShopper development chat on 2026-10-28.
